name: St. Vincent and the Grenadines
headline: St. Vincent and the Grenadines: +2.4% growth in 2025, 0.9% inflation, debt 108% of GDP
sections: St. Vincent and the Grenadines is a $1.2 billion economy (2025), the world's 202nd-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.4% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $23K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 3.9% of GDP (2025).

Consumer prices rose 0.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 5.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 18.0% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 41.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 108% of GDP (2025), a very high level that has risen from 82% in 2020. The general government balance is −13.0% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −16.4% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Net FDI inflows were 8.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 134% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 71.4 years (2024). Population: 111 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
